title_en: Li Xingying v. Shanghai RT-Mart Supermarket — dispute over compensation for damage to stored baggage
keywords_en: civil; dispute over deposit contract; second instance; intermediate people's court; Shanghai; natural person; legal person; Contract Law; distinction between deposit contract and loan-for-use contract; burden of proof for loss of items in self-service locker; whether supermarket fulfilled management duty; dismissal of claims; supermarket bag storage; self-service locker; loss of items; guarantee
full_text_en:
Li Xingying v. Shanghai Da Run Fa Co., Ltd., Yangpu Branch and Shanghai Da Run Fa Co., Ltd. — dispute over compensation for property damage from bag storage

Plaintiff: Li Xingying, female, 66 years old, retired employee, currently employed at Shanghai Air Travel Service, residing at No. ... Shuangyang Road, Shanghai.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Guizhuang, attorney at Shanghai Liting Law Firm.

Defendant: Shanghai Da Run Fa Co., Ltd., Yangpu Branch. Address: No. ... Huangxing Road, Shanghai.

Person in charge: Luo Jianzhong.

Defendant: Shanghai Da Run Fa Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. ... Gonghexin Road, Shanghai.

Legal representative: Xu Renyu, Chairman.

Agent ad litem for the two defendants: Zhou Zhiming, attorney at Shanghai Shenda Law Firm.

The plaintiff, Li Xingying, filed a lawsuit with the Yangpu District People's Court of Shanghai against the defendants, Shanghai Da Run Fa Co., Ltd., Yangpu Branch (hereinafter referred to as Da Run Fa Supermarket) and Shanghai Da Run Fa Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Da Run Fa Company), concerning a dispute over compensation for property damage arising from bag storage at the supermarket. The Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court, considering that this case had a significant impact within its jurisdiction, decided to hear the case at first instance pursuant to Articles 19 and 39 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

The plaintiff, Li Xingying, alleged: When the plaintiff went shopping at the defendant Da Run Fa Supermarket, she deposited her bag at the self-service storage cabinet No. 22 provided by the store, inserting a 1-yuan coin as instructed. When the coin came out from the coin return slot, a password slip bearing the number 1250719748 was ejected from above the coin slot, and a compartment door near the plaintiff's chest automatically opened. The plaintiff then placed a black leather bag (containing a tour group payment of RMB 4,660 she had just received and her personal money of RMB 650, totaling RMB 5,310) and an umbrella into that compartment, and proceeded to shop. After shopping, the plaintiff entered the password according to the instructions on the slip, but the compartment door would not open. She then sought assistance from a staff member of Da Run Fa Supermarket. After being asked to write down the names of the items stored in the compartment and the amount of money, a staff member used a key to open the compartment the plaintiff had indicated, but found it empty. That evening, the plaintiff reported the incident to the police and made a statement. The plaintiff later attempted to resolve the matter with Da Run Fa Supermarket and Da Run Fa Company, but to no avail. The plaintiff asserted that by requiring consumers to deposit their belongings in the self-service storage cabinets provided by the supermarket, a deposit contract was formed between the parties, and the supermarket should bear responsibility for the safekeeping of consumers' deposited property. Because Da Run Fa Supermarket was overly reliant on the safety and reliability of the self-service storage cabinets it provided to consumers and was negligent in management, the money and items the plaintiff deposited in the cabinet were lost. The plaintiff requested the court to order the two defendants to compensate her for economic losses of RMB 5,310, and to bear the litigation costs.

The defendants, Da Run Fa Supermarket and Da Run Fa Company, argued: It is true that the plaintiff shopped at Da Run Fa Supermarket on that day, but shopping and bag storage are not necessarily related; not all consumers need to store bags. The password slip provided by the plaintiff only indicates that the storage compartment was once opened by the plaintiff, but it does not prove that the plaintiff actually stored any items inside, let alone that the stored items were a bag, an umbrella, and a large sum of money. Furthermore, the self-service storage cabinet used by the plaintiff was provided free of charge by Da Run Fa Supermarket for consumers to store small items. The relationship formed between the parties is one of gratuitous loan for use. Da Run Fa Supermarket has clearly informed consumers of the usage methods and precautions for the self-service storage cabinets. For large items and valuable money and belongings carried by consumers, Da Run Fa Supermarket also provides a manual storage service. Since the self-service storage cabinet itself was not damaged, Da Run Fa Supermarket and Da Run Fa Company have no fault in the alleged loss of the plaintiff's items and bear no civil liability for compensation. The plaintiff's claims should be dismissed.

After pre-trial evidence exchange and court proceedings, the Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court confirmed the following facts, which were not disputed by either party:

Da Run Fa Supermarket is an affiliated enterprise of the defendant Da Run Fa Company.

On the afternoon of November 1, 2000, the plaintiff, Li Xingying, shopped at the defendant Da Run Fa Supermarket and used the self-service storage cabinet provided by the store. At around 5:30 p.m., after finishing shopping, Li Xingying approached a staff member of Da Run Fa Supermarket with a password slip numbered 1250719748 from the store's self-service storage cabinet. She stated that before shopping, she had deposited a leather bag (containing a tour group payment of RMB 4,660 she had just received from her employer, Shanghai Air Travel Service, and her personal funds of RMB 650, totaling RMB 5,310) and an umbrella in the storage compartment of self-service storage cabinet No. 22, and that she could not open the compartment. When the staff member opened the compartment door indicated by Li Xingying, it was found to be empty. The staff member informed Li Xingying that the compartment she had indicated did not match the compartment number shown on the password slip she held. However, when the staff member opened another compartment that corresponded to the number on the password slip, it was also found to be empty. That evening, Li Xingying reported the incident to the Wujiaochang Town Police Station of the Yangpu Branch of the Shanghai Public Security Bureau.

During the proceedings, the following issues were in dispute between the parties:

Issue One: Whether the leather bag, the items inside it, and the umbrella were placed into the self-service storage cabinet.

The plaintiff, Li Xingying, argued: At around 3:00 p.m. on November 1, 2000, after receiving a tour group payment of RMB 4,660 from her employer, Shanghai Air Travel Service, she took a bus and arrived at the defendant Da Run Fa Supermarket at around 4:00 p.m. Her actions were continuous without any intermediate stops. Therefore, it should be confirmed that she had placed the aforementioned money and items into the supermarket's self-service storage cabinet.

In support of this, the plaintiff submitted the following evidence:

Evidence 1: A password slip numbered 1250719748 from Da Run Fa Supermarket's self-service storage cabinet, to prove that Li Xingying had indeed stored a bag at Da Run Fa Supermarket.

Evidence 2: An inquiry record dated November 1, 2000, from the Wujiaochang Town Police Station of the Yangpu Branch of the Shanghai Public Security Bureau, to prove that Li Xingying had indeed reported the incident to the police, and to show the process of her dealings with Da Run Fa Supermarket.

Evidence 3: Two delivery orders from Da Run Fa Supermarket, to prove that Li Xingying had indeed shopped at Da Run Fa Supermarket on that day.

Evidence 4: A temporary payment slip from Shanghai Air Travel Service and a certificate issued by Shanghai Air Travel Service on August 30, 2002, along with the testimony of Yu Hong, the cashier of Shanghai Air Travel Service, to prove that Li Xingying, as a business representative of Shanghai Air Travel Service, had indeed received a tour group payment of RMB 4,660 at around 3:00 p.m. on November 1, 2000, from the cashier at the former Nanshi Business Department of Shanghai Air Travel Service, Room 615, No. 617, Zhongshan South Road, Shanghai.

The defendants, Da Run Fa Supermarket and Da Run Fa Company, did not dispute the authenticity of the above evidence submitted by the plaintiff, Li Xingying, but argued that this evidence could not prove that Li Xingying had placed the leather bag, its contents, and the umbrella into Da Run Fa Supermarket's self-service storage cabinet.

The defendants, Da Run Fa Supermarket and Da Run Fa Company, submitted the testimony of Xu Qinhua, former head of the Reception Section of Da Run Fa Supermarket, to explain the process of the complaint made by the plaintiff, Li Xingying, and how it was handled.

Issue Two: What legal relationship is formed between a consumer and the supermarket when a consumer uses the supermarket's self-service storage cabinets for storing items? If items deposited by a consumer in a self-service storage cabinet are lost, is the supermarket liable for compensation?

The plaintiff, Li Xingying, argued: The self-service storage cabinets are provided by the supermarket to attract consumers to shop in its store while at the same time ensuring the safety of the store's goods. This is a storage service derived from shopping. The relationship between the parties in this case is one of a deposit contract. Due to the fault of the defendant Da Run Fa Supermarket, or its failure to fulfill its management responsibilities, her deposited property was lost. Therefore, Da Run Fa Supermarket should bear civil liability for compensation.

The defendants, Da Run Fa Supermarket and Da Run Fa Company, argued: Da Run Fa Supermarket provides self-service storage cabinets free of charge for the convenience of consumers. The relationship formed regarding the use of these cabinets is one of a gratuitous loan for use. The self-service storage cabinets provided by Da Run Fa Supermarket are of good quality, and Da Run Fa Supermarket has clearly informed consumers of the usage methods and precautions, fulfilling its legal obligation to inform. The existing evidence can only prove that the plaintiff used Da Run Fa Supermarket's self-service storage cabinet, but cannot prove that the plaintiff actually placed her items inside the cabinet, let alone prove that the items she claimed were lost in that cabinet. Therefore, Da Run Fa Supermarket is not liable for compensation.

In support of this, the defendants, Da Run Fa Supermarket and Da Run Fa Company, submitted the following evidence:

Evidence 1: Testimony of Li Hepeng, Deputy Sales Manager of Shanghai Huaming Electronic Metal Cabinet Factory. Li Hepeng testified in court that the self-service storage cabinets used by Da Run Fa Supermarket are products of that factory. These products are marked with "Operating Steps" and "Bag Storage Instructions" upon leaving the factory. The passwords used consist of ten digits, with the first two digits indicating the number of the storage compartment within the cabinet, and the remaining eight digits being randomly combined, with no repetition possible in up to 100 million times. The storage compartments within each self-service storage cabinet are arranged from left to right, numbered from the top left corner vertically downwards. The products have passed tests conducted by the China Shanghai Testing Center and have not been subject to quality disputes.

Evidence 2: A set of photographs showing Da Run Fa Supermarket prominently displaying bag storage information. The text under the title "Precautions for Free Bag Storage Cabinet" reads: 1. Keep the password slip properly and do not show it to others; 2. Do not store items worth over RMB 200, cash, mobile phones, leather bags, and other valuables; 3. Self-service bag storage is on a self-service basis; the store is not responsible for any loss; 4. Do not leave bags overnight; any consequences of overnight storage are your own responsibility.

Evidence 3: Several internal work regulations and registration forms of the Reception Section of Da Run Fa Supermarket, to explain the internal management of the self-service storage cabinets. The main contents of the regulations include: For compartments that cannot be opened by normal password entry due to various reasons, staff, with the consumer's consent, shall first fill out an emergency compartment opening form, then use the key to open the compartment in the consumer's presence, and check whether the items match the consumer's description.

The plaintiff, Li Xingying, did not dispute the authenticity of the above evidence submitted by the defendants, Da Run Fa Supermarket and Da Run Fa Company, but argued that she was not aware of the password composition method of the self-service storage cabinets as described by the witness Li Hepeng, and that Da Run Fa Supermarket had not informed her of it.

Regarding the issues in dispute, the Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court found the following:

The coin-return type self-service storage cabinets involved in this case were purchased by the defendant Da Run Fa Supermarket from Shanghai Huaming Electronic Metal Cabinet Factory in October 1999. At that time, the store purchased 21 units of self-service storage cabinets, each consisting of 24 storage compartments, and 1 unit consisting of 16 storage compartments, all installed in the store. Each unit of self-service storage cabinet is marked with "Operating Steps" and "Bag Storage Instructions." The "Operating Steps" read: For storing: 1. Close any open door; 2. Insert coin; 3. Take password slip, do not show password to others; 4. Place bag into compartment; 5. Close door. For retrieving: 1. Enter password; 2. Remove items; 3. Close door, compartment door can only be opened once. The "Bag Storage Instructions" read: 1. Users should carefully read the "Operating Steps" and "Bag Storage Instructions"; those unfamiliar should consult a supervisor before operation. This store practices self-service bag storage, and the user bears all responsibility; 2. Before storing bags, first close any open compartment door, then insert coin to store bags; 3. Coin insertion is required to open the door for bag storage. Keep the password slip safe for retrieving bags. Password can only open the door once; 4. Cash and valuables must not be stored; 5. Please retrieve your items by 10:00 p.m. on the same day. Additionally, Da Run Fa Supermarket also provides a "Large Item Storage" service at its service counter.

During the trial, the judges conducted an on-site inspection at the defendant Da Run Fa Supermarket. The inspection confirmed that the compartment door described by the plaintiff, Li Xingying, as "automatically opening near my chest" was Compartment No. 3 within self-service storage cabinet No. 22. The first two digits of the password slip for Compartment No. 3 should be "03," but the first two digits of the password slip held by Li Xingying were "12." Upon opening all compartments of cabinet No. 22, the compartment corresponding to the password slip with the first two digits "12" was Compartment No. 12, which was located on the bottom-most layer of the entire cabinet unit (near the feet). During the on-site inspection, Li Xingying acknowledged that she had seen the "Operating Steps" and "Bag Storage Instructions" on the self-service storage cabinet on the day of shopping.

The Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court held:

Regarding disputed issue one. Reviewing the evidence submitted by the plaintiff, Li Xingying, it can only prove that at around 3:00 p.m. on November 1, 2000, she received a tour group payment of RMB 4,660 from the travel agency; and that over an hour later, she shopped at the defendant Da Run Fa Supermarket and used the supermarket's self-service storage cabinet. The evidence submitted by Li Xingying is insufficient to prove that when she used the self-service storage cabinet, she placed a leather bag containing RMB 5,310 and other items into the storage compartment.

Regarding disputed issue two. A contract is an agreement between parties to establish, modify, or terminate a civil relationship, and it represents the consistent expression of the parties' intention. Article 365 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China states: "A deposit contract is a contract under which the depositary keeps the deposited item delivered by the depositor and returns it." Article 367 states: "A deposit contract is established upon the delivery of the deposited item, unless otherwise agreed by the parties." According to the above legal provisions, a deposit contract is a real contract, meaning that the establishment of a deposit contract not only requires a consensus between the depositor and the depositary on the deposit of the item, but also requires the depositor to transfer possession of the deposited item to the depositary. The defendant Da Run Fa Supermarket, as a large supermarket, provides consumers who come to shop with two bag storage options: manual storage and self-service storage cabinets. On the self-service storage cabinets of Da Run Fa Supermarket, "Operating Steps" and "Bag Storage Instructions" are printed. Through the contents of the "Bag Storage Instructions" stating that "this store practices self-service bag storage, and the user bears all responsibility" and "cash and valuables must not be stored," Da Run Fa Supermarket has clearly communicated to consumers its intention to only provide the self-service storage cabinets for consumers' use, without assuming responsibility for the safekeeping of items stored in the cabinets. After seeing the express instructions on the self-service storage cabinets, the plaintiff, Li Xingying, still chose to use the self-service storage option, where she bears her own responsibility, instead of manual storage. This indicates that Li Xingying did not wish to deliver her items to Da Run Fa Supermarket for safekeeping, but only wished to temporarily store them using the supermarket's self-service storage cabinets. Therefore, the parties did not reach a consensus to form a deposit contract. Furthermore, by following the operating steps of the self-service storage cabinet through the human-machine dialogue of "inserting coin, coin returned, password slip ejected, compartment door automatically opened, storing items, closing compartment door," Li Xingying directly obtained the right to use the self-service storage cabinet and achieved the purpose of storing her items. In this process, Li Xingying's items were not transferred to the possession of Da Run Fa Supermarket, nor did Da Run Fa Supermarket receive the items deposited by Li Xingying. Li Xingying merely used the self-service storage cabinet to continue to control and possess her own items. Since Da Run Fa Supermarket did not receive the deposited items, it was unable to perform its duty of safekeeping. Therefore, the essential element for the establishment of a deposit contract—the transfer of possession of the deposited item—is absent. Consequently, the relationship formed between the parties regarding the use of the self-service storage cabinet is not a deposit contract but a loan-for-use contract.

Article 18, paragraph 1, of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Consumer Rights and Interests states: "Business operators shall ensure that the goods or services they provide meet the requirements for the protection of personal and property safety. For goods or services that may endanger personal or property safety, they shall provide consumers with truthful explanations and clear warnings, and explain and indicate the correct methods of using the goods or receiving the services, as well as methods for preventing harm." The defendant Da Run Fa Supermarket, by printing the "Operating Steps" and "Bag Storage Instructions," has informed consumers of the correct method of using the self-service storage cabinets and has provided truthful explanations and clear warnings about matters that may endanger consumers' property safety. Based on the testimony of witness Li Hepeng and the fact that there were no signs of tampering with the compartment doors of the self-service storage cabinets at the time, it can be determined that the items lent by Da Run Fa Supermarket were free from defects and possessed the necessary functionality for use. Da Run Fa Supermarket has fulfilled its statutory obligations as a business operator regarding the self-service storage cabinets it lends free of charge to consumers. Article 5 of the Contract Law states: "The parties shall observe the principle of fairness in determining each party's rights and obligations." Article 6 states: "The parties shall observe the principle of good faith in exercising their rights and performing their obligations." The on-site inspection proved that the compartment corresponding to the password slip held by the plaintiff, Li Xingying, was not the same as the compartment she claimed to have placed her leather bag in. Under these circumstances, Li Xingying cannot prove that she actually placed the alleged money and items into the self-service storage cabinet, nor can she prove that the alleged loss of items was caused by a quality problem with the self-service storage cabinet itself, nor can she prove that the alleged loss of items was caused by any intentional act or gross negligence on the part of Da Run Fa Supermarket in providing the storage service. Therefore, Li Xingying's request that Da Run Fa Supermarket and the defendant Da Run Fa Company bear compensation liability for the alleged loss of items lacks factual basis and legal grounds and cannot be sustained.

In conclusion, on October 10, 2002, the Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court rendered the following judgment:

The claims of the plaintiff, Li Xingying, are dismissed.

Court acceptance fee of RMB 222 shall be borne by the plaintiff, Li Xingying.

After the first-instance judgment, the Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court further pointed out to the parties: Currently, many supermarkets, in addition to providing manual storage services to consumers, also offer intelligent self-service storage cabinet services. This is a good thing that not only facilitates consumers who shop at the supermarket but also saves operating costs for the supermarket. However, because the self-service storage cabinet service is a product of modern business concepts and new technology, it breaks through the traditional scope of deposit and storage, forming a new type of loan-for-use relationship between businesses and consumers, thereby giving rise to this dispute arising from a consumer's use of a self-service storage cabinet. In this case, although the defendants, Da Run Fa Supermarket and Da Run Fa Company, prevailed, one point needs to be clarified: Compared to consumers, business operators hold a position of strength with substantial financial resources and should naturally provide more people-oriented services to consumers, doing their utmost to "satisfy consumers and reassure them." This is the business philosophy that modern operators should consciously follow. In relation to this case, if the supermarket could change the name of the "self-service storage cabinet" to better reflect the loan-for-use relationship formed between the supermarket and consumers through its use, misunderstandings could be reduced; if the storage compartments and password slips of the self-service storage cabinets could clearly display the compartment number, it might prevent consumers from placing items in the wrong compartment; if the supermarket could use existing technology to install electronic monitoring equipment in front of the self-service storage cabinets, then it would be clear whether the items allegedly lost by the plaintiff were placed in the cabinet, and if so, by whom they were taken and how. Supermarkets should not be satisfied with merely providing written precautions to consumers. They must continuously improve their service levels, strengthen the management of intelligent self-service storage cabinets to make them more perfect, and strive to create a more convenient, safe, and comfortable service environment for consumers.

The defendants, Da Run Fa Supermarket and Da Run Fa Company, sincerely accepted this suggestion from the Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court and indicated that they would definitely learn from this case and effectively improve their service to consumers.

After the first-instance judgment was pronounced, neither party appealed, and the judgment became legally effective.
